info.name: Ghar Ka Sathi — Backend API
info.description:
Full API collection for the Ghar Ka Sathi backend (User panel, Service Provider panel, Admin panel).

HOW TO USE:
1. Import this file AND 'postman_environment.json' into Postman, then select the 'Ghar Ka Sathi - Local' environment (top-right dropdown).
2. Make sure the backend is running (npm run dev) and MONGO_URI points to a live MongoDB.
3. Run 'Auth > Admin Login' first — it auto-saves {{adminToken}}.
3b. Mobile login flow is two steps: 'Auth > Check Mobile' (before the OTP is even sent — just tells the client whether this number is new) then 'Auth > Verify OTP' (after the client verifies the OTP with Firebase). Check Mobile never creates a record; Verify OTP is what actually logs the user in and creates one if new.
4. 'Auth > Verify OTP' needs a REAL Firebase phone-auth idToken, which you will not have out of the box. Easiest options:
   a) In Firebase Console > Authentication > Sign-in method > Phone > add a test phone number, sign in with it from a client app, and paste the resulting idToken here.
   b) Ask your backend dev to seed a test User/ServiceProvider directly in MongoDB and hand you a JWT for {{userToken}} / {{providerToken}} — this is what was used during development testing.
5. Once you have userToken/providerToken, run requests top-to-bottom within each folder — IDs (categoryId, providerId, bookingId, userId, complaintId) auto-save into collection variables via each request's Tests script, so later requests fill in automatically.
6. Admin-only routes need {{adminToken}}; user-only need {{userToken}}; provider-only need {{providerToken}}.

request.description: Simple liveness check — should return {"status":"ok"}.

Call this the moment the user taps "Send OTP", BEFORE actually triggering Firebase's OTP send. Only checks whether the phone number is already registered — never creates anything. Returns { "newUser": true|false }. Store this on the client and use it after OTP verify succeeds to decide navigation (new -> Registration/Profile Setup, existing -> Home).

Client verifies phone OTP with Firebase, then sends the resulting idToken here. Backend verifies it, finds-or-creates the User, returns our JWT. Needs a REAL Firebase idToken (see collection description for how to get one for testing).

request.description: Works with either {{userToken}} (if you own the booking) or {{providerToken}} (if assigned) — swap the Authorization value to test both.
Run this next in the happy path (do NOT run Cancel/Reject below first, or this booking will already be in a terminal state).
Fails 400 if no price was quoted yet (accept with a price first). Needed before Payments and Add Review below will work.
Only works once booking status is completed (run Mark Completed above first).

ALTERNATE ENDING — only run this on a booking that's still pending/accepted/in-progress. If you already ran Mark Completed above on {{bookingId}}, create a fresh booking first (re-run 'Create Booking') before testing this, otherwise it will correctly fail with 400.
ALTERNATE ENDING — same caveat as Cancel Booking above: test on a fresh booking, not one already completed/cancelled.
Needs RAZORPAY_KEY_ID/SECRET configured in .env, else returns 503. Booking must already have a price quote.

request.description: These three fields come from the Razorpay Checkout success callback on the client — cannot be fabricated for testing without a real gateway transaction.
Booking must be status "completed" first. Splits price into commission (per category) + provider payout, credits provider earnings.
Works with userToken or providerToken, whichever is on that booking.
Also broadcasts in real time over Socket.io to room booking:<id> — REST is enough for functional testing.
